subject: geography

moments.title: River Murray Waters Agreement
moments.who: New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia and the Commonwealth
moments.body: After decades of state rivalry over Murray-Darling water, the four governments sign a sharing agreement. The River Murray Commission is created to oversee allocation.
moments.takeaway: Australia's federal system left water as a state matter — until the basin's scale required intergovernmental cooperation.

moments.title: Millennium Drought peaks
moments.body: The Millennium Drought (around 1996-2010) reduces Murray-Darling flows to record lows. The river mouth at the Coorong silts up; salinity rises sharply; whole irrigation industries collapse. The basin contributes around 40% of Australia's agricultural output.
moments.takeaway: Climate variability had been managed by storage; sustained drought exposed over-allocation.

moments.title: Basin Plan
moments.who: Murray-Darling Basin Authority and the Commonwealth
moments.body: Statutory plan to recover 2,750 GL/year of environmental water by 2024. Buybacks of irrigation entitlements, infrastructure efficiency programmes. The plan is contested by states and irrigation communities; reviews and adjustments have continued.
moments.takeaway: Water reallocation between agricultural and environmental uses is politically expensive — and difficult to enforce when monitoring and compliance fall short.

now.title: Drought, fire, fish kills
now.body: Mass fish deaths at Menindee (2018, 2019, 2023) brought the basin's stress to national attention. The 2019-20 'Black Summer' fires and the 2022-23 La Nina floods illustrate the swings. Climate projections suggest declining mean flows and more extreme variability.
now.open_questions: Can a basin plan survive a hotter, more variable future? The Productivity Commission's reviews have repeatedly flagged implementation problems.

reflection: Water management in an arid basin is the hardest geographical problem in the Australian federation. The Murray-Darling case shows what happens when allocation outpaces the resource — and how slowly institutions adjust.
